passages.title: The Freshman Challenge
passages.body: Hi! My name is Adam and I'm a freshman at senior high school. Going from junior high school to senior high school is a really big challenge, and my first week was a little confusing. First, I had to think carefully about which courses I wanted to take. The school adviser helped me choose the suitable ones: maths, English, chemistry, world history, and Chinese. I know that Chinese is a very difficult language, but I hope to be fluent when I graduate. My adviser also recommended that I should sign up for advanced literature, because I like English and I'm good at it. I had to choose extra-curricular activities, too. I tried to join the school football team, but the coach told me that I didn't play well enough. Obviously, I was unhappy, but I won't quit. I'll find a way to improve on my own so that I can make the team next year. Instead, I joined a volunteer club. Every Wednesday, we hand out food to homeless people in the community. I know I'll have to study harder and get used to being responsible for a lot more. Still, I'm happy to be here, and I'll be well prepared for whatever comes in the future.

options: He had to make many new choices, such as courses and activities.

questions.answer_text: He had to make many new choices, such as courses and activities.
questions.explanation: 首段说他要仔细选课、选课外活动,新选择多,所以感到 confusing。

options: Because Adam likes English and is good at it.

questions.answer_text: Because Adam likes English and is good at it.
questions.explanation: 原文:because I like English and I'm good at it。

questions.answer_text: To be chosen as a member of the team.

passages.title: A Letter of Advice
passages.body: Dear Worried Friend, You wrote that you are very worried about your friend, Chen Lei. I understand quite well that you feel anxious. You think that your friend plays computer games too often and spends too much time online. I recommend that you talk to your friend about his behaviour. It is not unusual for teenagers of your generation to be attracted to computer games and the online world. But spending too much time online is unhealthy, and it makes it very difficult to focus on other things in life. Some students even become addicted to the Internet and cannot concentrate on school and family life. I think you should encourage your friend to try new hobbies. Why not discuss the problem together? I am sure he will listen to you, since you are his good friend. All the best, Susan Luo

options: He spends too much time playing computer games online.
He has no friends at school.

questions.answer_text: He spends too much time playing computer games online.
questions.explanation: 信中说 your friend plays computer games too often and spends too much time online。

questions.answer_text: Talk to the friend and encourage him to try new hobbies.
questions.explanation: 她建议 talk to your friend about his behaviour 并 encourage him to try new hobbies。

questions.stem: According to the letter, why is spending too much time online a problem?
options: It is unhealthy and makes it hard to focus on other things.
It makes people fluent in English.
questions.answer_text: It is unhealthy and makes it hard to focus on other things.
questions.explanation: 原文:unhealthy, and it makes it very difficult to focus on other things in life。

options: Because his parents asked him to.

questions.explanation: 原文:I am sure he will listen to you, since you are his good friend。

passages.title: Choosing the Right Club
passages.body: At senior high school, there are many clubs for students to join. Each club has its own activities. In the Ballet Club, students learn new movements and dance together. In the Nature Club, they grow plants and work in a greenhouse. Members of the Debate Club enjoy discussing different topics, and they think and speak quite quickly. The Volunteer Club is also popular: its members help old people and clean up parks at the weekend. So how can you choose a suitable club? First, think about what you are interested in. If you love animals and plants, the Nature Club may be a good choice. Second, think about what you are good at. A student who speaks well may do well in the Debate Club. Finally, remember that a club should be fun, not just useful. The right club can help you make new friends and learn something new outside class.

questions.answer_text: Grow plants and work in a greenhouse.

questions.explanation: 原文:First, think about what you are interested in。

questions.answer_text: How to choose a suitable school club.
questions.explanation: 全文介绍各社团并给出选社团的方法,主旨是如何选合适的社团。

passages.title: Managing Your Time at Senior High
passages.body: Senior high school students often feel that there is never enough time. They have more homework, more subjects, and more extra-curricular activities than before. Being responsible for so much can be a real challenge. So how can teenagers manage their time well? The answer is to make a schedule. A schedule is a plan that shows what you will do and when. First, write down the most important tasks, such as homework and review. Then decide how much time each task needs. It is also wise to leave some free time for sports or hobbies, because all work and no play is not healthy. When you follow your schedule, you will feel less anxious and get more done. Good time management will not happen in one day, but if you keep trying, it will soon become a useful habit.

questions.answer_text: They have more homework, subjects and activities.

passages.title: First Impressions
passages.body: So this is it — senior high school at last! I'm not very outgoing, so I felt a little anxious on my first morning. I wanted to make a good first impression, but I kept thinking: Will I make any friends? What if no one talks to me? My first maths class was difficult, but the teacher was kind and friendly. He even told us a funny story, and everyone laughed so much! I found most of my classmates and teachers friendly and helpful. In the afternoon, we had a chemistry class in the science lab. The lab was new, but the guy next to me talked the whole time, and I couldn't concentrate on the experiment. By the evening, I felt much better. This morning I was worried that no one would talk to me, but I was wrong. I didn't feel awkward or frightened at all. I miss my old friends, but I believe I'll make new ones here. I feel much more confident than I did this morning. I think tomorrow will be a great day!

She did not like the school.
questions.answer_text: She is not very outgoing and worried about making friends.

passages.title: Growing Up and Taking Responsibility
passages.body: Being a teenager is not always easy. As we grow up, we have to be responsible for more and more things. At home, we should help our parents and take care of ourselves. At school, we are responsible for our own studies and behaviour. Some teenagers think that being responsible means losing their freedom, but this is not true. In fact, responsibility and freedom go together. When you show that you can be responsible, adults trust you more and give you more freedom. For example, if you always finish your homework on time, your parents will not worry about your studies. If you keep your promises, your friends will believe in you. Of course, no one becomes responsible in a single day. We all make mistakes, but mistakes are a normal part of growing up. What matters is that we learn from them and keep trying to do better.

questions.explanation: 原文:At school, we are responsible for our own studies and behaviour。

questions.answer_text: Adults trust you more and give you more freedom.
